device.description: quadruple 8-bit low-power voltage-output DAC with 3-wire serial interface (CLK, DATA, EN), single/double-buffered modes and power-down
device.note: slas138b.pdf (SLAS138B) p.1 (pinout), p.2 (terminal functions), p.3 (data interface, single-buffer mode), p.4 (Figures 1-2), p.5 (double-buffered mode, Figure 3), p.6 (Figure 4), p.7 (control register Table 2, shutdown Table 3, serial input decode Table 4), p.8 (power-on reset Table 5), p.10 (recommended operating conditions: VDD 2.7-5.5 V, timing), p.13 (Figures 6-7)

registers.name: INA
registers.note: DACA input latch (A1 A0 = 00, Table 4 p.7); power-on value not given (0 used)

registers.name: INB
registers.note: DACB input latch (A1 A0 = 01, Table 4 p.7); power-on value not given (0 used)

registers.name: INC
registers.note: DACC input latch (A1 A0 = 10, Table 4 p.7); power-on value not given (0 used)

registers.name: IND
registers.note: DACD input latch (A1 A0 = 11, Table 4 p.7); power-on value not given (0 used)

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: control register, bits in serial order MODE, RNG A-D, SIA-SID, ACT (Table 2 p.7, Figures 1-4); power-on MODE 0, RNG 1, SI 0, ACT 0 (Table 5 p.8)

commands.name: Data word (single-buffer mode)
commands.note: start bit 1, RS = 1, A1 A0, D7-D0 (Figures 2 and 4); MODE = 1: the output updates on the twelfth CLK falling edge (p.3)

commands.name: Data word (double-buffer mode)
commands.note: MODE = 0 (power-on default): the input latch is written; the outputs update on EN falling (p.5)

commands.name: Control word (single-buffer mode)
commands.note: start bit 1, RS = 0, MODE, RNG A-D, SIA-SID, ACT; once set MODE cannot be cleared (p.3), so the MODE bit is ignored; outputs update at the end of the word (Figure 1)

commands.name: Control word setting single-buffer mode
commands.note: MODE = 1 selects single-buffered mode; the data written so far is latched to the DACs at the end of this word (Figure 2)

commands.name: Control word (double-buffer mode)
commands.note: MODE = 0; the datasheet latches the control word on EN falling (Figure 3, note 14), the model stores it at once

commands.name: Idle / word synchronization
commands.note: leading zeros are skipped until a start bit (twelve zeros regain word synchronization, Figure 1)

protocol.note: p.3, p.5: DATA is clocked in on CLK falling edges while EN is high (EN is the active-high frame pin; CLK idles low in Figures 1-4 -> mode 1); words are 12 bits: a start bit 1, RS (1 = data, 0 = control) and 10 bits; zeros before a start bit are skipped; any number of words per EN-high window (stream)

ldac.note: double-buffered mode: all DAC outputs update on the EN falling edge (p.5)

pages: p.1-2 (pins), p.3-6 (data interface and Figures 1-4: word layout start bit, RS, A1 A0, D7-D0 / MODE, RNG A-D, SIA-SID, ACT), p.7-8 (control register, shutdown, decode, power-on values), p.10 (ROC and timing)
notModeled: analog: voltage outputs DACA-DACD, reference inputs REFA-REFD, x1/x2 range (RNG bits stored only)

the word layout (a start bit then RS) is read from the timing figures; the datasheet text has no bit table. RS spans the first two clocks of a data word (drawn high) and is a high bit followed by a low RS bit in a control word

double-buffered mode latches the control word (RNG, SIx, ACT) on EN falling (note 14 p.12); the model stores it when the word completes. A range change in double-buffered mode changes the output on EN falling (analog only)
in single-buffer mode EN is tied high; an EN falling edge in that mode still updates all outputs in the model (no effect when the outputs are already current)
shutdown: ACT, SIA-SID and the HWACT pin (Table 3) only switch the analog outputs off; the bits are stored, HWACT is not modeled
power-on contents of the input and DAC latches are not given (0 used); all DACs are shut down at power on (ACT = 0, analog only)
variants: TLV5621I only (industrial temperature range); the TLC5620 (5 V, LOAD/LDAC interface) has a separate datasheet
